overall: Board violated the Open Meeting Law by withholding executive session minutes on a purchase whose purpose had ended and by creating insufficiently detailed minutes; it also mishandled the complaint response.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board withheld executive session minutes on Little Harbor Country Club purchase after a records request, though the purchase had closed.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, to the extent there are additional sets of minutes for executive sessions in which the Board discussed the purchase of the Little Harbor Country Club, the Board must release those minutes, or portions of those minutes that relate to the purchase of the Little Harbor Country Club.

allegations.summary: Not raised in the complaint; AG reviewed the October 5, November 9, and November 16, 2021 executive session minutes and found them insufficiently detailed.
allegations.key_passage: Based on our review of the October 5, November 9, and November 16, 2021, executive session minutes, we find that the minutes merely contain a list of motions made and votes taken without summarizing any discussions.

allegations.summary: Board did not formally respond to the Open Meeting Law complaint within the required 14 business days, and did not take or describe remedial action.
allegations.key_passage: Finally, we note that the Board did not properly or timely respond to Ms. Kinniburgh’s Open Meeting Law complaint.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Amend the October 5, November 9, and November 16, 2021 executive session minutes, and any other related minutes that are similarly insufficient, in accordance with the guidance provided.
Release to the complainant any additional executive session minutes pertaining to the purchase of the Little Harbor Country Club, subject to appropriate redactions.
Certify to the Attorney General's office compliance with this order within 60 days of the determination.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of an intent to violate the Law.
